facts.claim: Voyager 1 was launched by NASA on September 5, 1977, from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
As of January 2026, Voyager 1 is approximately 24.9 billion kilometers from Earth.
Voyager 1 is traveling at about 17 kilometers per second relative to the Sun.
Voyager 1 entered interstellar space on August 25, 2012, becoming the first human-made object to do so.
Voyager 1's distance from Earth as of 2026 is about 166.5 astronomical units (AU).
Voyager 1 carries the Golden Record, a 12-inch gold-plated copper disk containing sounds and images of Earth.
Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, was launched 16 days earlier, on August 20, 1977.
The Voyager 1 spacecraft weighs about 722 kilograms, including propellant.
Voyager 1's primary mission was to study Jupiter and Saturn, which it flew by in 1979 and 1980 respectively.
Voyager 1 discovered volcanic activity on Jupiter's moon Io in 1979.
Voyager 1's power source is a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG), which produces about 245 watts at launch, degrading over time.
As of 2026, Voyager 1 still communicates with Earth using a 23-watt radio transmitter, with a signal delay of about 22 hours and 40 minutes each way.
Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, the boundary where the solar wind meets interstellar medium, at about 121 AU from the Sun.
The Voyager 1 mission is expected to last until approximately 2030, when its RTG will no longer have enough power to run any instruments.
Voyager 1 was designed and built by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) under NASA, with key scientists including Carl Sagan on the Golden Record committee.

hook_ideas: Open with the sounds of space or the Golden Record's 'Sounds of Earth' to immediately connect to the human element.
Use a live 'distance ticker' animation showing kilometers increasing in real-time.
Start with the 22-hour radio signal delay: 'Today, if you shout at Voyager 1, you'll have to wait two days for your voice to arrive.'
Show the 'Pale Blue Dot' image, taken by Voyager 1 at 6 billion km, and quote Carl Sagan's reflection.
misconceptions: Misconception: Voyager 1 has left the solar system. In reality, it has entered interstellar space but still remains within the Sun's gravitational sphere of influence (Oort cloud).
Misconception: Voyager 1 is the fastest human-made object. Several NASA probe (e.g., Parker Solar Probe) have achieved higher solar-relative speeds, but Voyager 1 is the farthest.
Misconception: The Golden Record contains engraved images that are meant to be read by aliens. It is primarily a time capsule for humanity, with instructions for playback included.
